adoption_case: Solar milling and IoT moisture sensors
transcript: Interviewer: Please tell me about your business.
Aisha: We mill rice from smallholders around Bunkure. Power was killing us—diesel cost and outages.
Interviewer: Tell me the story of adopting solar and sensors.

Aisha: In 2020, a big client rejected a batch for moisture issues. That loss pushed us. We compared diesel gen sets vs. hybrid solar. Vendor showed payback under 24 months if we controlled drying with sensors.
Interviewer: Biggest hurdles?
Aisha: Finance first. Bank wanted collateral we didn’t have. We used a vendor lease with maintenance. Skills too—operators were scared of the dashboard, so we made Hausa guides and peer mentoring.
Interviewer: Outcomes?
Aisha: Downtime fell by half, fuel spend dropped 40%, rejection fell from 8% to 2%. Clients now ask for us.
Interviewer: Any trade-offs?
Aisha: On cloudy weeks we still ration loads. Also, replacement batteries are expensive.
Interviewer: What led you online?
Chinedu: Lockdown and border delays hit us. Customers were already on WhatsApp, so we built a simple storefront and used broadcast lists.
Interviewer: Hurdles?
Chinedu: Logistics pricing was chaotic. Broadband in the market is weak; we switched to night uploads and compressed images.
Interviewer: Outcomes?
Chinedu: Online sales went from 0 to 25% of revenue in 8 months. Returns dropped after we standardized specs.
Funmi: Cash was leaking. POS gave us visibility, and with bookkeeping we saw weekday slump and shifted promos.
Interviewer: Constraints?
Funmi: Fees and chargebacks. We negotiated a blended MDR and trained staff on reconciliation.
Interviewer: Impact?
Funmi: Revenue grew ~18% and shrinkage reduced a lot.
Musa: Clients want precision. We tested CNC to cut rework.
Interviewer: Hurdles?
Musa: Skills and power. We paired a trainee with a vendor engineer. Used UPS to ride out short outages.
Interviewer: Results?
Musa: Lead time down 20%, but scrap still high during design handover.
Titi: We were losing rolls. Barcodes made stock counts objective.
Interviewer: Challenges?
Titi: Resistance from store keepers; we did incentives and weekly dashboards.
Interviewer: Outcomes?
Titi: Stock-outs reduced and we caught slow-moving items sooner.
Sade: We needed traceability for ISO. LIMS gave audit trails.
Interviewer: Constraints?
Sade: Data privacy and staff buy-in. We segmented access and ran drills.
Interviewer: Impact?
Sade: Fewer specimen mix-ups and faster results release.
Emeka: Instagram blew up demand. We integrated a local courier API.
Hurdles?
Emeka: Fraud and fake alerts. We used payment links and held shipment till confirmation.
Outcomes?
Emeka: Sales doubled in festive season; returns manageable.
Halima: Farmers prefer cash. Agents helped onboarding.
Constraints?
Halima: Trust—some thought fees were hidden. We did demos at market days.
Impact?
Halima: Faster payouts and fewer lost receipts.
Bayo: Clients suffer stockouts. We bolted a forecasting module to existing POS.
Hurdles?
Bayo: Data access—merchants reluctant to share granular data. We created opt-in cohorts with clean-room style aggregates.
Impact?
Bayo: Early pilots show 12% stockout reduction in test stores.
Zainab: We sell frozen fish. Before, outages spoiled stock.
Hurdles?
Zainab: Upfront cost. Vendor offered installment with maintenance.
Impact?
Zainab: Spoilage down 60% and we extended hours.
Ahmed: Fuel is our biggest line. Routing cut zig-zag.
Hurdles?
Ahmed: Drivers feared surveillance. We reframed as bonus eligibility based on safe driving and OTP deliveries.
Impact?
Ahmed: Fuel per drop fell 15%, on-time up to 92%.
Ngozi: Parents demanded flexibility. We set up LMS with recorded classes.
Hurdles?
Ngozi: Data costs for students. We negotiated zero-rating windows with an ISP pilot.
Impact?
Ngozi: Completion rates improved and we enrolled students outside Enugu.
Tunde: Brooders were overheating. Sensors alerted us earlier.
Hurdles?
Tunde: Vendor lock-in—proprietary gateway. We negotiated data export and a buyout clause.
Impact?
Tunde: Mortality down modestly so far.
Maryam: We saw what sold and ordered smarter.
Hurdles?
Maryam: Staff rotation—new hires struggled. We created a laminated quick guide.
Impact?
Maryam: Stock-outs fell and we reduced dead stock.
Ifeoma: We tracked energy by line and shifted heavy loads to solar windows.
Hurdles?
Ifeoma: Policy risk on import duties; we diversified suppliers.
Impact?
Ifeoma: Energy cost per unit fell 18%, and fewer burnouts.
Seyi: We joined two aggregators. Discovery improved.
Hurdles?
Seyi: Commissions high and brand diluted. We pushed direct ordering with coupon inserts.
Impact?
Seyi: Sales grew but margins tight; kitchen utilization smoother.
Idris: Quicker quotes and receipts.
Hurdles?
Idris: Backup—lost a phone once. We enforced cloud backups.
Impact?
Idris: Faster payments and fewer disputes.
Ruth: Fish died during heat waves. Aeration scheduling helped.
Hurdles?
Ruth: Power cost; we used timers and off-peak.
Impact?
Ruth: Survival rate up modestly.
Uche: We track tools across sites now.
Hurdles?
Uche: Cybersecurity—client required audits. We implemented MDM and SOC-lite.
Impact?
Uche: Losses down and utilization up.
Aminat: Short videos work. POS helps reconciliations.
Hurdles?
Aminat: Trust—some customers fear scams. We offer pay-on-delivery in-town.
Impact?
Aminat: Early signs of growth with repeat buyers.
